newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares continue downward path.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares continue downward path.

text.p: Shares closed generally lower in Tuesday trading on the Nigerian bourse and dealers blamed economic recession for months of bearish sentiment on the market.
The all-share index dropped to 7967.51 from 7974.38 on Monday.
Traders said economic problems continued to drive investors to sell and said that, despite the release of money last week to government ministries and other bodies, a turnaround was not in sight.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) was down 20 kobo at 59.30 naira. Lever Brothers fell 30 kobo to 22.50 naira and African Petroleum finished 20 kobo down at 47.80 naira.
Traders put some positive movements in the banking, brewing and food sectors down to speculation.
Union Bank rose to 9.15 naira, up 10 kobo, the same amount as brewing company Guinness which ended at 9.10 naira.
Oil miller P S Mandrides strengthened to 7.40 naira, up 13 kobo, and healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham closed five kobo up at 5.80 naira.
